transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-03-12 15:00 UTC | Duration 90 min | Recorded by Fireflies
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Clara Nguyen (Redwood SE), Diego Ramos (Redwood PMM), Maya Lopez (Aurelia VP Product), Ethan Brown (Aurelia ML Eng), Priya Singh (Aurelia Head Eng), Liam O'Connor (Aurelia Sales Ops)

[00:00] Samir: All right everyone, thanks for carving out time. This is the SE/AE enablement — I'm Samir, AE, and Clara is our SE. We'll run through messaging, a short competitor section, then do two demo roleplays.
[00:22] Clara: Hi all, quick note: the goal is practical — snippets you can use on calls, and a repeatable demo flow. Expect some rough edges, we want feedback.
[00:38] Maya: Sounds great, we're excited — we want the team to be confident in Dedicated vs Hosted conversations.
[00:52] Diego: I'll take notes on playbook gaps. Also, logging the common procurement asks so we can include in the doc.
[01:10] Clara: First, the one-liner: Redwood is a developer-first inference platform optimizing for production economics — predictable latency, cost controls, and unified runtime across hosted, dedicated, and private. Say it fast and then unpack.
[01:40] Ethan: Quick question: what do you mean by production economics? Is that just cheaper tokens?
[01:52] Samir: Good q. Not only token cost — it's about throughput, batch/caching savings, predictable tail latency, and fallback routing so apps don't go down when a model's busy.
[02:20] Clara: Example script: "If your SLAs need <300ms p95, we recommend Dedicated or pinned hosted variants with autoscale; if you need lower TCO with variable latency, host with our batching + quantization profiles."
[02:50] Priya: Procurement will ping on compliance: KMS, SOC2, logs. What's our standard reply?
[03:05] Samir: We have SOC2 Type II, KMS integrations, audit logs. For Private we offer customer-managed KMS and VPC peering. I'll flag Diego to attach the security deck.
[03:30] Clara: Quick competitor bullets — Anthropic: safety-first messaging; OpenAI: strong model portfolio and brand; Cohere: embeddings focus; AWS SageMaker: integrated infra for enterprises. Our angle: neutral model catalog + production controls + predictable serving economics.
[04:00] [roleplay prep] Samir: Okay, roleplay 1 — Clara as AE, Samir as customer, Ethan will observe. We'll simulate price/latency objection.
[04:20] Clara (roleplay AE): "I hear you're concerned about both latency and cost — can you quantify p95 target and QPS?"
[04:35] Samir (roleplay): "We're targeting 200ms p95 and 50 qps for peak times, and budget is a big constraint."
[04:50] Clara: "Great — in that regime we'd recommend Dedicated with autoscale and prefix caching. That gives predictable tail latency and lets you use quantized models to get cost down. We can run a short benchmark for your workload."
[05:12] Samir: Feels good — maybe add a line about fallback to cheaper variant.
[05:25] Clara: noted.
[05:40] [06:00] Diego: small note, use the phrase 'predictable spend' rather than 'cheaper' — procurement likes predictability.
[06:20] [06:45] Roleplay 2 prep: Clara to demo live call flow — show streaming, function/tool calling, and fallback policy.
[07:10] Clara: I'm going to share the demo script link now: shorturl.at/redwood-demo (note: placeholder). Starting with a simple chat prompt, then toggle to dedicated config and show latency differences.
[07:45] [08:15] Demo (live): Clara: "Ok initiating call: 'Summarize clinical notes and extract patient contacts'" — starting stream...
[08:50] Samir: transcript shows some stutters — the copy got 'clinical nots' in the ASR, just a note that demos occasionally show mis-typed proper nouns.
[09:20] Ethan: in real demos we need safeguards so PHI isn't accidentally shown; we must highlight SOC2 + private.
[09:40] Clara: agreed; show the redacted UI view and explain retention policies.
[10:05] [10:40] Dialogue on tooling hooks: Clara explains rollouts, canary flows, A/B, automatic fallback to smaller model family if N+1 fails.
[11:15] Priya: How do you recommend handling KV cache priming for clinical prompts?
[11:30] Clara: Prime on startup, but be explicit about cache TTL and eviction. We can provide a config template.
[12:02] [12:45] Mis-transcription example: speaker label swapped — shows as Speaker 3 sometimes. Not critical.
[12:55] [13:30] Diego: objection script — procurement likes to ask about vendor lock-in and model portability. How do we answer?
[13:45] Samir: emphasize model catalog openness and ability to route by model variant; customers control pinning and can export configs. Not full model portability but operational portability.
[14:10] Clara: practice line: "We don't lock you to a single model — our routing layer and model catalog let you choose and pin versions; you own the prompts and rollout policy."
[14:35] [15:00] Roleplay 3: procurement scenario — Maya to roleplay procurement lead.
[15:10] Maya (roleplay): "Legal says we need data residency and auditable logs for 7 years. Can you do that?"
[15:30] Clara: "Yes — Private deployments offer customer-managed storage, and we can increase retention in our audit logs; we'll work with your compliance team on exportability."
[15:55] Liam: note: ask about e-Discovery exports — add to documentation.
[16:20] [16:50] Samir: quick micro-coaching: avoid deep technical rabbit holes when AE is present; SE should surface complexity but keep deliverables clear.
[17:10] Clara: Understood — I'll stick to 'what it accomplishes' vs 'how.'
[17:30] [18:00] Demo hiccup: stream latency spike in demo environment, Clara improvises by switching to cached response to show graceful degradation.
[18:40] Ethan: that was great improv — shows resilience.
[19:00] [19:35] Diego: PMM note — capture that fallback example as a one-liner for emails.
[20:00] [20:30] Deeper technical Qs: Priya asks about kernel selection and quantization compatibility with customer models. Clara: high-level only — runtime picks kernels per architecture; we recommend tested quant profiles for common families.
[21:05] Samir: if the customer asks for exact quant steps, route to Solutions Engineering for a tech deep dive.
[21:35] [22:00] Objections bank: the team lists common ones: "we use OpenAI", "we need SOC2 now", "we can't share data with third-party", "cost is unpredictable".
[22:30] Clara: for 'we use OpenAI' — response: OpenAI has brand power; we compete on production controls and price predictability; offer benchmark invites.
[23:00] Roleplay wrap up and feedback from audience — Maya: liked demo flow but wants more explicit procurement lines.
[23:30] Samir: Action items recap — I'll send the security deck + cheat sheets, Clara will run shadow demos, Diego will produce email snippets.
[24:00] [24:30] Closing: quick Q/A, then schedule follow-up enablement session focused on procurement playbook.
[24:50] End of recording (note: Fireflies truncated transcript after 25 minutes mark; full 90m session recorded but this export includes main segments and highlights).

References mentioned briefly in call: security deck (link to be shared), quickstart repo (shorturl.at/redwood-qs placeholder), demo script (internal), fallback playbook (to be compiled).

Notes about transcription: occasional ASR errors on product names (KV cache -> 'K V cache', Redwood Dedicated -> 'Read wood dedicated'). Keep that in mind when sharing internally.
